picks.style: greek victory ode, lyre and aulos, chorus answering a soloist, stately triadic sway, questioning, mounting
picks.why: 'In which of your glories did you most delight, blessed Thebe?' — a chain of 'or when...' questions, including Zeus falling as a snow-shower of gold at midnight.

picks.style: greek choral lament turning to praise, kithara and low drone, grave massed voices, solemn, ebbing, resigned
picks.why: 'We die all alike, but our fates are diverse' — winged Pegasus throwing Bellerophon, and sweetness beyond measure awaiting a bitter end.

picks.style: hymnic greek invocation, lyre with struck bronze, bright high voice over drone, radiant, ceremonial, unhurried
picks.why: Night-long fire prodding the air with fragrant smoke, then 'Mother of the Sun, Theia of many names' — a hymn opening in the middle of an ode.

picks.style: roman comic patter song, tibia pipes and hand drum, fast wry male voice, chattering, cheeky, accelerating
picks.why: The rant against busybodies — 'they know what Juno talked about in conversation with Jupiter; that which neither is nor is likely to be, do these fellows know.'

picks.style: latin street-wisdom song, plucked lyre and clacking percussion, dry rueful baritone, mid-tempo, shrugging, worldly
picks.why: 'I bought myself an enemy with my talent, and sold my friend' — the whole economics of lending money to a friend in six lines.

picks.style: baroque ode for music, harpsichord continuo and strings, dramatic tenor with chorus, hammering short lines, infernal then radiant
picks.why: Orpheus at the gates of hell with its clipped catalogue — 'Fires that glow, Shrieks of Woe, Sullen Moans, Hollow Groans' — Pope wrote this one to be sung.

picks.style: georgian philosophical anthem, chamber organ and strings, calm baritone opening to chorus, stately, resolving, luminous
picks.why: 'All Nature is but Art, unknown to thee; all Chance, Direction which thou canst not see; all Discord, Harmony not understood' — anaphora built for a final chorus.

picks.style: comic english catch, fiddle and bassoon, gruff jovial bass, bouncing tetrameter, boisterous, barking
picks.why: Pope's great dane writing a letter to a lapdog: 'We Country Dogs love nobler Sport, and scorn the Pranks of Dogs at Court.'

picks.style: english evening ode, solo flute and viola, soft high female voice, unrhymed and floating, dusk-lit, hushed
picks.why: 'By fairy hands their knell is rung, by forms unseen their dirge is sung' running straight into the Ode to Evening — Collins at his best twice over.

picks.style: ode for music, baroque orchestra with shifting solo voices, dramatic contrasts, startled then desolate then rising
picks.why: The Passions each seizing the lyre in turn — Fear recoiling at his own sound, Anger striking one rude clash — a score in the words already.

picks.style: persian-flavoured pastoral eclogue, oud and frame drum with strings, warm female voice, refrain-driven, courtly, lilting
picks.why: The shepherd girl carried off by a king, still turning back to look at her flock, with the refrain closing each turn of the story.

picks.style: english christmas hymn, church organ and brass, full congregational chorus, bright, jubilant, ringing
picks.why: 'Hark how all the Welkin rings' — the first version of the carol everyone knows, before it was smoothed into 'Hark! the herald angels sing'.

picks.style: methodist hymn, harmonium and low strings, fervent solo tenor opening to chorus, building, released, radiant
picks.why: 'I woke; the Dungeon flam'd with Light; my Chains fell off, my Heart was free' — the most electric stanza Wesley ever wrote.

picks.style: open-air revival hymn, fiddle and tambourine with rough chorus, urgent baritone caller, driving, exhortatory, plain
picks.why: 'Outcasts of Men, to You I call, harlots and publicans, and thieves!' — a hymn that names its congregation and dares the world.

picks.style: english parlour song, spinet and recorder, light bright soprano, skipping trochees, cheerful, fireside
picks.why: 'Little inmate, full of mirth, chirping on my kitchen hearth' — a clean, complete address to a cricket, and it scans like a nursery tune.

picks.style: comic english glee, bassoon and fiddle, dry deadpan baritone with croaking chorus, jaunty, wry
picks.why: The jackdaw on the steeple watching church, army, physic and law go round below — 'and says, what says he? Caw.'

picks.style: georgian moral air, guitar and viola, gentle tenor, ballad meter, twilight, tender
picks.why: The glow-worm given 'a modicum of light, proportion'd to his size' — a small joke that turns into a small theology.

picks.style: irish rebel song, bodhran and fiddle, defiant male voice, driving, angry, marching
picks.why: 'Who strikes when he's struck, and takes when he starves, in the eyes of the Lord is no rebel' — one coherent furious lyric, not a collage.

picks.style: ancient greek epitaph chant, single lyre over low drone, cool unhurried voice, slow, circular, stone-still
picks.why: The bronze maiden on the tomb of Midas, speaking so long as water runs and trees put forth leaves — the only candidate, but a real epigram.
